professional_summary: The narrow same-day scan yielded four relevant papers: glasma transport of hard probes, quark-level strangeness conservation, multihadron fragmentation-function evolution, and ML-assisted holographic-QCD calibration. The main themes are pre-equilibrium transport, strange-hadron correlations, multiscale factorization, and physics-constrained inverse modeling.
strongest_paper_summary: Glasma transport gives concrete heavy-flavor and jet observables for testing pre-equilibrium effects.

papers.title: Transport of hard probes in the glasma
papers.abstract: Studies jet and heavy-quark transport through pre-equilibrium glasma fields with classical Yang-Mills and light-front quantum methods; finds enhanced anisotropic transport, potentially measurable D-Dbar decorrelations, and moderate R_AA effects.

papers.title: Strangeness suppression, the phi meson and Lambda-antLambda spin correlations from exact strangeness conservation at the quark level
papers.abstract: Imposes exact strangeness conservation on quarks in finite causal clusters and describes strange-hadron yields in pp and p-Pb while linking phi suppression to Lambda-antLambda spin-correlation dilution.

papers.title: Evolution of multihadron fragmentation functions with nonperturbative behavior
papers.abstract: Develops evolution for multihadron fragmentation functions with multiple invariant-mass scales, separating extra-scale dependence from ordinary fragmentation evolution.

papers.title: Thermal properties of the rho meson from a machine-learning-improved holographic QCD model
papers.short_authors: Jia-Jie Jiang, Han Tang, Danning Li, Lang Yu
papers.abstract: Uses a neural-network-assisted inverse calibration of a soft-wall AdS/QCD background against lattice screening masses, then computes rho spectral functions and quasi-normal modes, obtaining a dissociation estimate near 168 MeV.
